text:
Priya: Heads up — Ashford (customer) just pinged support: dedicated pool throughput dropped ~40% this morning at 08:12 UTC. p50 looks fine, p95->p99 tail increased and request queue grew. Can runtime team triage?

Ethan: forwarding their support log here, they said it started after a deploy but not sure which. Support attached request IDs and a short dump.

perf-bot: ALERT: asg-dedicated-ashford average tokens/s decreased from 3200 -> 1900 between 2026-03-16T08:10 and 2026-03-16T08:18 UTC. p99 latency increased 3.7x.

Mike: assigning to me to start. @Zoe can you pull the node-level metrics for that pool (GPU util, PCIe, NVMe IO) around the window? I want to see if it's infra or model-related.

Zoe: grabbing metrics now. Initial look: GPU util unchanged (~78%), but host-side CPU sys time spikes on the serving nodes in that pool and we see elevated page faults on 3 of 12 hosts. NVMe latencies are a bit noisy on two hosts.

Priya: support said customer pinned model:v2-quant. They also said they had an internal burst load at the same time (short-lived). Could be a batching regression under burst?

Mike: good catch. Two parallel asks: (1) can someone repro a short burst locally with model:v2-quant to see if batching or kernel selector regresses? (2) collect full runtime traces (kv cache hit/miss, batching stats, kernel selection) for the window. I'll add temporary trace hooks if needed.

Lina: I can run a quick repro harness with synthetic burst (1000 concurrent small requests) on a staging pool that uses v2-quant. Will run with both latest kernel selector and the previous stable release. ETA ~30m.

Ethan: forwarded Ashford request IDs: rid: ash-20260316-8a2, ash-20260316-8b7. They included this snippet from their client logs: ```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-ID: ash-20260316-8a2
latency: 0.42s
...
``` but server reported 1.8s internal for same token count.

Mike: thanks. If staging repros, include env var ENABLE_CONTINUOUS_BATCH_LOG=1 so we can capture batch sizes per second. Also log kernel selection version: `runtime --kernel-version`.

Zoe: adding note: three hosts with pagefaults were running an older kernel on host OS (5.15.x) compared to rest (6.1.x). Could be a driver interaction with NVMe. I'm spinning up a node-level iostat and dmesg capture.

Priya: quick product ask — Ashford is on a paid SLA. We should prepare a short incident summary for them (timeline + next steps) within 2 hours. I'll draft once we have root cause or mitigation.

perf-bot: TRACE: batch-size histogram (ash-pool) around window: mode=1, mean=1.4 -> mean=2.8 during spike; queue length increased from 3->18. KV cache hit rate dipped 2%.

Mike: interesting — mean batch size increased, p99 spiked. That suggests queueing behavior changed (maybe batching timeout or stale kernel path causing longer tail). Lina, results?

Lina: repro complete. With latest kernel selector (commit ab12f) we see the same p99 bump under short bursts on v2-quant. With the previous selector it stays stable. Attaching quick output: ```staging run: 1000 reqs in 30s -> p50 0.21s p95 0.38s p99 1.72s (latest selector)
previous selector -> p50 0.20s p95 0.35s p99 0.45s```

Mike: bingo. Sounds like the selector is choosing an incompatible kernel variant for quantized path under burst (maybe switching to a slower fallback). I'll bisect the selector change set.

Zoe: On infra — we still should patch the 3 hosts' kernels & NVMe firmware to rule out IO tail, but kernel-selector repro looks like the primary cause.

Priya: mitigation for customer now? Can we force a selector fallback or pin model variant while we fix selector?

Mike: yes — we can hotpatch routing: add a model-variant override for Ashford to `v2-quant-stable` (previous kernel mapping). Lina can prepare the variant and I can push routing override.

Lina: prepared variant `v2-quant-stable` and tested on staging — pushes consistent p99. If Priya approves I can stage the rollout to Ashford-only route.

Priya: approve, roll it out and tell support to confirm client-side latency normalizes. I'll send the customer note template.

Ethan: rolling to Ashford now. Support will monitor and report back within 10m.

perf-bot: ROLLBACK: route override applied to customer ashford (routes/ashford -> v2-quant-stable).

Zoe: infra patch in progress for 3 suspicious hosts (kernel upgrade + NVMe firmware). ETA 45m, non-disruptive.

Mike: bisecting selector now. Early candidate looks like commit 0f3c9 which adjusted heuristic for short sequences to favor larger-tile kernels. Might have caused slowdown on quant path. I'll open the PR to revert that heuristic pending tests.

Lina: quick CI numbers: selector revert candidate restores p99 in our stress tests. I'll attach perf graphs to PR.

Priya: great. Once we have PR + infra patch plan, I'll finish customer summary (timeline, mitigation, next steps). Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Ethan: Ashford confirmed latency dropped back to baseline after override. Closing loop — will keep monitoring.

Mike: follow-ups: 1) PR to revert 0f3c9 (assigned to me). 2) add canary test for bursty batching on quantized models (Lina). 3) infra kernel/fw patch (Zoe). 4) incident writeup (Priya/Ethan). I'll update this thread with links to PR and postmortem.

perf-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (temporary mitigation applied).
